cues.en: Now when we are implementing the binary tree using linked list implementation, we have said that we
have two main types of the tree traversal.
So we have breadth first search and depth first search.
Now in case of depth first search we have three types preorder in order and post order.
But when it comes to breadth first search we have level order traversal.
So in this lecture we are going to look at level order traversal.
So I'm just going to go ahead and quickly recap the how level order traversal work.
So it's going to be very quick.
So in this case we have a binary tree like this.
So here we have a three level for this binary tree.
So this means that when we are visiting the elements we are going to start from the first level.
Then continue to visit all elements in the second level.
Then we are going to continue to visit all elements in the third level.
So in case of this binary tree, the order is going to be like this.
First we are visiting n1, then n2, then we continue to N3, then we are going to continue in four
and five and six and in seven.
So that's going to be the order of the traversal in case of level order traversal for this tree.
Now let's look at the implementation.
So when we have the array implementation of the binary tree like this it's going to be like this.
So in one which is root is located at index of one.
Then based on the formula that we have provided n2 is the left child of the N1 is going to be at the
index of two.
Then we have N3 as the right child of the N1, which is going to located at the index of three.
And it continues like this.
Now here the first thing that we will do, we are going to declare the level order method.
Then we are going to write the loop like this.
So as we mentioned before, in the zeroth index we will not have any node.
That's why our loop will start from one which is going to be the first index.
Then it will continue until we reach the last used index.
We know that in the last use index property we have the last cells index.
So that's why we will continue like this.
And in each step we are going to increase the I by one.
Then the next step is we are going to check that if the current cell's value is not undefined, we are
going to go ahead and print out that cell's value to the console, which means that we have visited
that node.
Because sometimes if we delete some nodes from here, it's possible that some cells will be empty.
That's why we have to check with this if condition and not visit that cells.
So in this case, if we run level order traversal for this binary tree, the first node is going to
be n1.
Then it will continue to n2.
Then in the next iteration it will continue to N3.
Then it will continue N4.
Then it's going to continue to N5 then and six and N7.
So as you can see first we are visiting first level, then the second level and the third level.

Now let's look at the time complexity of this method.
So first we have a loop.
So this loop will take on time complexity because we are visiting all nodes of the binary tree, which

And then we have if condition and this if condition.
